description: Returns what one signal is (its catalog entry, the same object List signals returns for it) and every ticker matching it, live or on any past date with `asof`: a screen on that one signal. Returns `catalog` (what the signal is) every time. Booleans list their matches with no `condition`; every other type lists them only with one, typed like the signal: ">70" (numeric), "<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ" (timestamp), ">=YYYY-MM-DD" (date), "=ETF" (string); without it you get the catalog entry and a `note`. Without `order`, a non-boolean sorts by its value in the direction the condition implies (`<` ascending, `>` descending). To know when each ticker started matching, use tickerbot_query_events with kind=signal, signal=<name>, transition=enter.

asof.description: Target moment as `YYYY-MM-DD` (that day's close) or an ISO timestamp (that intraday moment; daily-only signals then carry the previous session's close, never that day's): the same read as it stood then, unlimited depth. Full contract under As of a past date.

condition.description: Lists the matches of a non-boolean signal; without it the response carries the catalog entry and a `note` instead of `results`. The shape follows the signal's `type` in the catalog. Single bound, `<op><value>`. numeric: `>70`, `<=200`, `!=0` (operators `>`, `>=`, `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`). timestamp: an ISO instant, `<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` or `>=YYYY-MM-DD` (a bare date is midnight UTC). date: `>=YYYY-MM-DD` or `=YYYY-MM-DD`. string: `=ETF` or `!=ETF` (`=` and `!=` only; quotes optional). A relative window ("older than 15 minutes") is a `/v2/scan` query: `price_asof < now() - interval '15 minutes'`. Sending a condition with a boolean or custom signal returns 400 (it does not apply).

cursor.description: The previous response's `next_cursor`. Send it with the same params as the first page (`limit` may change); a page whose params differ is a 400 naming the param.

dir.description: Sort direction. Omitted: the direction the default order implies, else `desc`.

grain.description: Only with `asof`. Grain the past state is read at: `1m`, `1h`, `1d` or `auto` (default). `auto` blends: each signal comes from its freshest grain at or before the instant (minute, then hourly, then the last closed daily session), so nothing is refused for grain and no ticker is dropped; `_meta.blended` and `_meta.grains_present` say what contributed. Pin a grain for the fastest response: one grain is read instead of three, and every ticker is captured on the same clock. A signal the pinned grain does not store is a `400 interval_unavailable` naming the grains that carry it (`rsi_14`, fundamentals and valuation ratios are `1d`-only). `1m` and `1h` need a timestamp `asof`; with a bare date they are a `400 interval_unavailable`.

limit.description: Page size. Max 200 until 2027-01-12, then 100 (a larger value is clamped to the max, not an error; `next_cursor` pages the rest; see Deprecations).

order.description: Signal to sort by (or `ticker`). Omitted: a yes/no signal lists tickers A→Z; any other signal sorts by its value in the direction the condition implies (`<`/`<=` ascending, `>`/`>=` descending).

select.description: Signals each match carries beside `value`, e.g. `market_cap,sector`. `*` is every signal: the whole live row, or on an as-of read every signal the read's grain stores. An unknown signal is a 400, beside `*` too.

signal.description: A signal name. Booleans (e.g. `golden_cross`, `above_sma_50`) are detected automatically; every other type (numeric `rsi_14`, timestamp `price_asof`, date `earnings_date`, string `asset_class`) requires a `condition`. An object or list signal (`leadership`, `etf_holders`) has no `condition` form: the read returns its catalog entry and a `note`; screen on it with `POST /v2/scan`.

universe.description: Scope to a built-in universe (`top_10`, `top_100`) or one of your own, by id. An unknown one answers 200 with no results and its id in `not_found`.

name: tickerbot_get_signal
